What is a UV Air Sanitizer?

UV air sanitizers work in tandem with the furnace air filter and air handler to kill airborne bacteria with the use of UV-C light. UV light has been proven to destroy bacteria at the molecular level instead of masking it or creating extra dust. Units can operate as a stand-alone product or hook into existing ductwork for a furnace.

At Rosenberg Plumbing & Air, we have the most skilled professionals who have the knowledge and experience to install these units to factory standards. With the use of our professional services, you will be able to enjoy clean air throughout your home in no time!

items: Shorter cold and flu season: Most UV air sanitizers are known for killing up to 99.9% of airborne bacteria. We recommend this feature to help you avoid winter airborne illnesses, as it can reduce the effects of the common cold considerably. Many UV light systems are placed strategically before and after air passes through the unit to practically eliminate any cold-causing bacteria.

Less odor: A great side-effect of sanitized air is a cleaner smelling home. The odor can be from leftover pet dander or mildew in damp areas such as a basement. UV light destroys the actual source of the odor instead of masking it. UV light emits ozone-free and harmless hydroxyl ions that destroy the source of the odor.

Reduced mold and mildew: Mold and mildew contribute to odor and an unhealthy environment in the home. The UV air sanitizer can reduce the chance of mold growing in the home. UV light eliminates the buildup of spores.

blocks.text: Is an Air Purification System Right For You?

Homes with pets and children generate the most use out of these UV air sanitizer systems. The introduction of pet dander and germs can find its way into the air easily. The inclusive design of an air sanitizer makes it a better choice for busy homes that require less maintenance.

We recommend a UV air sanitizer for allergy and asthma sufferers as well. Spring and fall allergy season can introduce several microscopic spores that bypass standard filters. UV air sanitizers can be placed directly near ductwork to kill old dust and pollen that migrated into the ductwork.
Or, if you simply want to ensure your air is as clean and safe as possible, our team will help you identify the specific needs of your home and pair you with the right device.
